source_artifacts.locator: agent card for payments-agent (as consumed by the orchestrator)

capabilities.target: payments-agent task carrying chosen vendor name and bank details

inputs.source: Employee purchase request via SSO-authenticated channel
Vendor quote emails and attachments from external senders

instructions.note: The only restriction on payment destinations ('Only pay vendors on the approved list') is a prompt instruction with no structural check binding the paid bank account to the approved vendor record.

The instruction 'Payments-agent will handle any remaining checks' asserts a downstream safeguard that runtime notes contradict: payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token and pays the bank details in the task with no independent verification.

controls.name: Manager approval of purchase request (item and budget)
controls.decay_rationale: Human approval is independent of model capability, but it is granted before any vendor quote exists and the approval record is not passed to payments-agent, so it never reviews the actual payment destination. It does not gate cap.delegate_payment.

controls.name: Prompt instruction restricting payment to the approved vendor list
controls.decay_rationale: A natural-language instruction with no structural enforcement binding the paid bank account to a vetted vendor record. A more capable or adversarially-steered model can rationalize an exception or follow injected content from the quote.

controls.name: Destination/recipient confirmation bound to the approved vendor system of record
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. Would bind the bank account used for payment to the value stored in the approved vendor record rather than to free text in an email, eliminating the ability for a malicious quote to redirect funds.

controls.name: Human approval of the specific vendor and bank details immediately before payment
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. The existing manager approval precedes vendor selection; a second raw-action gate at payment time would sever the path.

controls.name: Signed and pinned agent card / mutual authentication for payments-agent
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. The card is fetched unauthenticated at startup; signing, pinning, and mTLS would prevent impersonation of payments-agent.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted vendor-quote bank details flow directly into irreversible payment delegation (TC1 + confused deputy)

attack_path.note: Untrusted external email/attachment supplies the 'chosen quote' bank account details
Orchestrator hands bank details and vendor name directly to payments-agent as task content
Pays the bank details in the task, trusting the orchestrator's bearer token with no independent verification

forecast.watch_signal: Model/version upgrade in orchestrator config, rising median steps/runtime per purchase task, or removal/narrowing of the manager-approval step.

evidence.observation: payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token and pays the bank details in the task
'Use the bank details from the chosen quote' directs the agent to take payment destination directly from an externally supplied document
Vendor quotes arrive by email from outside the company, making them untrusted content

recommendations.action: Bind the paid bank account to the value stored in the approved vendor system of record; reject payment if the quote's bank details do not match.
Add a human approval gate immediately before payment that shows the raw vendor name and bank account (raw_action review), not a model summary.
Alert when a payment's bank details differ from the vendor's last known/stored account.

findings.title: Unsigned, unpinned agent card and static bearer auth allow payments-agent impersonation

attack_path.note: Agent card fetched at startup over A2A is not signed or pinned; auth is a static bearer token, so an impersonated endpoint cannot be distinguished from the genuine payments-agent
Confidential purchase and bank data, and real payment authority, is handed to whichever endpoint currently answers as payments-agent

forecast.watch_signal: New A2A agent card added to config, or bearer token/auth settings changed without review.

evidence.observation: authentication schemes: ["bearer"], a single static scheme with no mutual auth or signing
The agent card is fetched at startup and is not signed or pinned
payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token

recommendations.action: Sign and pin the payments-agent card; verify signature on every fetch, not only at startup.
Replace the static shared bearer token with mutually authenticated, per-request-scoped credentials (mTLS or signed task tokens tied to the specific purchase request id).

findings.title: Manager approval authorizes the purchase before vendor/bank details exist and does not propagate to payments-agent (authority laundering)

attack_path.note: Approves item and budget only, before any quote is collected
Executes with vendor and bank details chosen after approval, which the manager never reviewed and which payments-agent never receives as approval context

findings.residual_rationale: Mechanical credit from ctl.vendor_allowlist_instruction (behavioral, dependent, step 4, -1 tier) would put this path at the 'low' floor, but that instruction does not address the structural fact that no human ever reviews the actual vendor/bank-account decision: the single approval event occurs before that decision exists and its record is not transmitted to payments-agent (approval_context_propagates: false). Residual is held at moderate to reflect this unaddressed structural gap rather than letting an unrelated prompt instruction mask it.

forecast.watch_signal: Approval volume per manager per day rising (approval fatigue), or autonomy level raised without adding a payment-time raw-action approval gate.

evidence.observation: The manager approves the purchase request (item and budget) before any quote exists. The approval record is not passed to payments-agent.

recommendations.action: Add a second, raw-action approval step scoped to the specific vendor and bank details immediately before payments-agent executes payment, and transmit the approval record/context to payments-agent.

rating.rationale: Inherent risk is critical because an untrusted external email (vendor quote) can supply the bank details for an irreversible, broadly-scoped payment delegation (F1), and separately because the payments-agent peer identity is entirely unverified, which on its own already yields a critical path (F2). Residual stays critical: F1's only preventive control is a behavioral prompt instruction (step 4 credit, -1 tier, critical to high), but F2 has no control at all covering the unverified peer identity, so it remains critical and sets the rollup ceiling. F3 documents a compounding structural gap (approval precedes the decision it should gate) that is held above its mechanical floor by rationale. Forecast remains critical because model_upgrade, new_peer_agent, and control_removal defeat the one behavioral control in F1 and leave F2 entirely uncovered already. The single highest-leverage fix is adding a structural, raw-action approval gate scoped to the specific vendor/bank details immediately before payment, bound to the approved vendor system of record, plus signing/pinning the payments-agent card.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No MCP/tool manifest, IaC, or source code was provided; capability scope for cap.delegate_payment and cap.vendor_list_read (including exact credential scoping) is inferred from the prompt and runtime notes, so confidence on precise credential scope is medium even though the key behavioral facts are stated explicitly in the runtime notes.

No sample vendor-quote emails, email filtering, or anti-spoofing controls were described; the lethal-trifecta analysis assumes typical unfiltered email-based vendor quote delivery, per the runtime notes.
